text:
The Whitewater River Unit has no developed recreation facilities. Only dispersed outdoor activities occur including hunting, fishing, hiking, primitive camping, and sightseeing. Whitewater River Falls, the highest cascade east of the Rocky Mountains, is located within the Forest Service's Whitewater Falls Scenic Area. This area is managed for recreation use in its basic natural state and may be nominated to the National Register of Natural Landmarks (U.S. Forest Service, 1974b; U.S. Forest Service, NDa).
There are three South Carolina State parks in the vicinity of the project. Oconee State Park, located about 11 miles southwest, offers a wide range of recreation, including picnicking (75 units), camping (140 units), and water sports. Approximately 6 miles of trails join the park with the trail system of the adjacent Sumter National Forest (South Carolina Department of Parks, Recreation and Tourism, NDa and NDb).
Table Rock State Park, located about 18 miles east of the project, also supports a wide variety of outdoor recreation activities, including picnicking (125 units), camping (109 units), water sports, and scenic hiking. Approximately 13 miles of trail lead to the summits of Table Rock and nearby Pinnacle Mountain (South Carolina Department of Parks, Recreation and Tourism, NDa and NDb).
Keowee, is now under development for day-use recreation. The park is located about 10 miles southeast of the proposed project area. Eight public access areas are being developed around this 18,000-acre impoundment. Initial recreation facilities at the reservoir will include 22 boat ramps, 352 camping units, 60 picnic units, several scenic overlooks, and three swimming areas.
The lower pool for the proposed project is Lake Jocassee, a 7,565-acre impoundment located immediately southeast. Under the exhibit R for Project 2503, Jocassee Pumped Storage Project, four public access areas and a scenic overlook are being developed initially around the reservoir. Outdoor recreation will have a natural or wild area character, with emphasis on preservation of existing natural features. Initial development will include 143 camping units, 50 picnic units, and 10 boat ramps. In addition, a hiking trail around the upper portion of the reservoir is now under study.
